acceptanceGrade: ACCEPT-WITH-ONE-ADVISORY. Application-grade for what this artifact is — a partial execution-remainder join plus a measured statement of what remains — and expressly not a leftover closure.

scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsAccepted: That the product law for DR-133's seven retained negative-test classes stays on provider-only-output-contract.v3; that NT-1, NT-2, NT-6 are capable of riding DR-G21's malformed/truncated/duplicate/EOF corpus and NT-4, NT-7 capable of riding DR-G20's final-authority and authority-escape properties, each under the gate's own recorded owner; that NT-3 and NT-5 are not capable of riding any live gate corpus and remain leftover-design; and that D-056 gates 2 and 3 do not hold today and become satisfiable only after a later D-086 successor names the riding classes at those gates the way DR-102's CC-1..CC-11 are named at DR-G21.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsNotAccepted: This ACCEPT does not close DR-133's leftover-design, does not discharge D-139's L item for DR-133, and does not make DR-133 D-056-eligible. Two of seven classes have no obligation at all, and the five that can ride are not yet named at their gates. DR-133 stays OPEN, not eligible in kind, not SATISFIED.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatItUnblocks: A D-086 successor of clearly bounded scope — amend the DR-G20 and DR-G21 entries to name the riding classes, add no new DR-G* row, settle nothing about NT-3 and NT-5. That is a materially lighter next act than the new-required-gate path v3 and v4 proposed.

advisories.title: The closestGateScan tombstone still redirects readers to a field deleted two versions ago
advisories.finding: closestGateScan remains the v4 string 'Superseded by g20Quoted / g21Quoted / classes.*.g20g21Join. The v3 short characterizations of G20/G21 are withdrawn.' Measured: no class in v6 has a g20g21Join key — that field was replaced by executionRemainder at v5. So the one field whose entire job is to tell a reader where content went sends them to something that does not exist, and does not mention otherGatesScan, which is where the gate scan actually lives. I named this in the repair text of CLAUDE-PONGJ-V5-SF1 and it was not done.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: On reflection the consequence is navigational rather than governance-bearing. The finding I actually charged at v5 was that the disposition table misreported what had been answered, and that is fixed: every remaining landedAt resolves. A reader misdirected by this note loses a few seconds and then finds otherGatesScan; no claim about the seven classes, the gates, or D-056 depends on it. Blocking a sixth version on a stale cross-reference string would not be proportionate.
advisories.repair: Delete the key, or rewrite it as 'Superseded by g20Quoted, g21Quoted, classes.*.executionRemainder and otherGatesScan.'

independence.otherReviewerHandling: Codex verdicts for v1 through v5 exist on disk; none was opened. The prompt reports Codex accepted v5 at 0/0, which I take from the prompt and do not rely on.
independence.priorPositions: Across this family I have rejected v1, v2, v4 and v5 and accepted v3. Both of my v5 blockers were the reason a sixth version exists, so accepting v6 risks accepting my own repairs on sight. I re-derived each from primary sources rather than from the disposition table: every quoted cell re-compared with ==, every per-class fragment resolved to the specific source field that carries it, the 22 live gate claims read again, and the key set diffed against v5 to rule out the kind of regression that made v4 fail.
independence.notEscalated: I did not charge the truncated disposition table, the proposedObligation wording, or the d056Gate3Test sentence, each of which I considered and recorded above. At version six the temptation to keep finding something is the failure mode to guard against, and none of those three would change what a later cycle does.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Thirteen attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Read the scope before recording this: what is accepted is a partial execution-remainder join plus a measured statement of what remains, not a closure. DR-133's leftover-design stays open, D-139's L item is not discharged, and the row stays OPEN, not eligible in kind, not SATISFIED. Both of my v5 blockers land in full. The artifact now denies in terms that it closes leftover-design or makes gates 2 and 3 hold, and a new owedLater block names the act that would move them — a D-086 successor amending the DR-G20 and DR-G21 entries so the riding classes are named there the way D-086's G21 entry names DR-102's CC-1..CC-11, adding no new DR-G* row and settling nothing about NT-3 and NT-5. NT-3 and NT-5 are withdrawn from the join entirely, marked not-capable-of-riding and leftoverDesign true with a reason naming what an obligation for them would have to exercise, and NT-6 is re-cited from retained evidence to the corpus fragment its siblings use. The three stale disposition pointers are gone and all seven remaining ones resolve against the document's own structure. Everything unchanged still verifies: 24 of 24 gate cells, the DR-133 evidence cell and both D-086 executes strings byte-exact, all four digests reproducing, seven class names matching the contract, and the 22-gate arithmetic holding at 20 plus 2. After the v4 cycle I checked the key set against v5 specifically for a repair paid for by deleting a landed one; nothing was lost and owedLater was added. The single advisory is that closestGateScan is still the v4 tombstone pointing at classes.*.g20g21Join, a field deleted two versions ago, instead of at otherGatesScan where the scan now lives; I named it at v5 and it was not done, but its consequence is navigational rather than governance-bearing and it does not block. Three further items I considered and declined are recorded in the verdict so the choices are auditable. What this unblocks is a D-086 successor of clearly bounded scope, which is a materially lighter next act than the new-required-gate path v3 and v4 proposed.
